entries.title: Unexpected shutdown (power loss, hard reset or crash)
entries.what: Windows restarted without shutting down cleanly. The PC lost power, the power button was held, the system froze and was reset, or it crashed with a blue screen.
causes: Power loss or unstable power supply (PSU, UPS, power strip)
Power button held / reset pressed after a freeze
Blue screen (then the stop code is filled in)
Faulty driver that froze the system
fix: Look for a Blue screen event (WER 1001) at the same time - if present, analyze the minidump
If there is no stop code: check PSU, UPS and cables, and temperatures (CPU/GPU)
Remove overclock/XMP to test stability
Update BIOS, chipset and graphics drivers

entries.title: Entering sleep
entries.what: The system is going to sleep. The message shows the reason (user, idle timer, button, lid).

entries.title: Resumed from sleep
entries.what: The system woke up from sleep or hibernation.

entries.title: Kernel started a shutdown or restart
entries.what: The kernel power manager began a shutdown, restart or update transition. Normal at every shutdown.

entries.title: Power source changed (AC / battery)
entries.what: The computer switched between mains power and battery.

entries.title: Connectivity state in standby changed
entries.what: Modern standby changed whether network is kept active while sleeping. Normal on laptops.

entries.title: Entering modern standby
entries.what: The screen turned off and the system entered modern standby. Normal on laptops and tablets.

entries.title: Exiting modern standby
entries.what: The system left modern standby (screen on). Normal.

entries.title: Session power state changed
entries.what: Internal power state transition logged by Windows. Normal.

entries.title: Firmware changed processor memory settings
entries.what: The BIOS/UEFI changed processor memory type range registers (MTRRs). Logged on many systems at boot or resume; harmless.

entries.title: Processor power management capabilities
entries.what: Informational boot record describing CPU power features. Harmless.

entries.title: CPU speed limited by firmware
entries.what: The BIOS/firmware is limiting processor speed, usually because of heat or a power limit. The PC runs slower than it should.
causes: CPU overheating (dust, dried thermal paste, failed fan)
Laptop running on battery or a weak charger
BIOS power limits or power plan settings
fix: Check CPU temperature under load
Clean fans/heatsink, renew thermal paste
On laptops use the original charger
Update BIOS; check power plan (High performance / Balanced)

entries.title: Processor power management capabilities
entries.what: Informational boot record listing CPU power-management features for each core. Harmless.

entries.title: Resumed from sleep (wake source)
entries.what: The system woke up. The message shows the sleep time, wake time and the wake source (device or timer).
fix: If the PC wakes up by itself: powercfg /waketimers and powercfg /devicequery wake_armed show the culprits

entries.title: Windows started
entries.what: The operating system started at the time shown in the message. Marks every boot.

entries.title: Windows shut down
entries.what: The operating system shut down cleanly.

entries.title: System time changed
entries.what: The system clock was changed (time sync, user, or after resume). The message shows old and new time.
causes: Dead CMOS battery if the jump is large at every boot
fix: If the clock is wrong after every power-off, replace the CMOS battery

entries.title: Registry hive access history cleared
entries.what: Windows cleared the access history of a registry hive while loading it. Routine housekeeping; harmless.

entries.title: Boot information
entries.what: Routine record written during startup (boot type, firmware, boot menu, virtualization-based security). Harmless.

entries.title: Event Log service started (system boot)
entries.what: Marks a system start.

entries.title: Event Log service stopped (clean shutdown)
entries.what: Marks a clean shutdown.

entries.title: Previous shutdown was unexpected
entries.what: At boot Windows found that the last shutdown was not clean. The message shows when the system went down.
causes: Power loss or power button held
fix: Look at events just before the time in the message
Check for Kernel-Power 41 and WER 1001 (blue screen) at the same boot

entries.title: Windows version at boot
entries.what: Records the Windows version and build at each boot.

entries.title: System uptime
entries.what: Daily record of how long the system has been running (in seconds).

entries.title: Computer name changed
entries.what: The NetBIOS name and DNS host name of this computer were changed.

entries.title: Shutdown/restart requested
entries.what: A user or a program asked Windows to shut down or restart. The message names the process, the user and the reason.
causes: Third-party tool (backup, UPS or disk-monitoring software, remote management)
fix: If a program restarts the PC unexpectedly, check its settings or scheduled tasks

entries.title: Reason given for unexpected shutdown
entries.what: A user entered a reason for the last unexpected shutdown (Shutdown Event Tracker on servers).

entries.title: Blue screen (BugCheck)
entries.what: Windows crashed with a stop error and restarted. The message contains the stop code and where the memory dump was saved.
fix: Read the decoded stop code below
Open the minidump (C:\Windows\Minidump) with WinDbg: !analyze -v names the driver
Update or roll back the named driver; update BIOS and chipset
Test RAM (Windows Memory Diagnostic or MemTest86)

entries.title: An event log was cleared
entries.what: Someone cleared one of the event logs (the message names the log and the user). Can be maintenance - or someone hiding tracks.
fix: Confirm who cleared it and why

entries.title: Event logging service shut down
entries.what: Logged at normal shutdown. Suspicious only if the system did not shut down at that time.

entries.title: Audit events were dropped
entries.what: Security audit events were lost because of a transport/queue problem.
fix: Reduce audit policy noise or increase log size

entries.title: Security log was cleared
entries.what: The Security audit log was cleared. The message names the account that did it.
fix: Verify the account and reason; unexpected clears should be investigated

entries.title: Security log is full
entries.what: The Security log reached its maximum size and is not overwriting events, so new audit events are lost.
causes: Log retention set to 'Do not overwrite'
fix: Increase the maximum log size or enable 'Overwrite events as needed' / archiving

entries.title: Event log automatic backup
entries.what: The log was full and was archived automatically.

entries.title: User logon/logoff notification
entries.what: Customer Experience Improvement Program record of a user logon (7001) or logoff (7002). Harmless.

entries.title: Winlogon notification subscriber unavailable
entries.what: A component (often SessionEnv) was not ready to handle a logon notification. Very common and harmless.

entries.title: Winlogon notification subscriber did not handle event
entries.what: A logon notification subscriber skipped an event. Harmless.

entries.title: Check Disk ran at startup
entries.what: Chkdsk ran before Windows started. The message contains the full result, including any repairs.
causes: Volume was marked dirty after a crash or power loss
fix: Read the message for 'Windows has made corrections' or bad sectors
If it repeats, check disk health (SMART)
